messages:
sophia: FYI customer reported a production spike after upgrading python SDK -> multiple duplicate requests + auth retries. They upgraded from 1.28.x to 1.31.x and saw a sudden billing jump. Repro steps and logs below.

sophia: Repro steps:
1) pip install redwood==1.31.0
2) simple client call in a loop: 
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=env.get('REDWOOD_KEY'))
for _ in range(3):
    resp = client.generate("short prompt")
    print(resp.status_code)
```
Observed: two requests per loop iteration, intermittent 401 then immediate retry causing duplicate tokens billed.

sophia: Logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-15T14:02:01.123Z INFO request id=abc123 status=200
2026-03-15T14:02:01.456Z WARN request id=def456 status=401 auth=missing-token header=none
2026-03-15T14:02:01.458Z INFO retrying request id=def456 attempt=1
2026-03-15T14:02:01.459Z INFO request id=def456 status=200
```

maria: Thanks, looking. Two quick asks: can you paste pip freeze from the env and the exact client init call? Also is the customer using connection pooling (requests.Session) or plain client per call?

sophia: pip freeze attached in ticket: redwood==1.31.0
sophia: client was single global client instance (no explicit Session). init: `RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))`

maria: I think this is related to the retry behavior change we shipped around 1.30 where we switched default retry on 401->refresh to optimistic immediate retry. In some auth edge cases that causes two billable requests: failing request then retried when token refresh race resolves.

maria: Quick mitigation: pin to 1.29.x until we patch, or set explicit RetryPolicy to disable immediate retries. Example: 
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient, RetryPolicy
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_retries=0))  # disable client-side retry
```
This keeps the app in control and avoids duplicate billing.

alex: Confirming — we changed default retry semantics to try to reduce latency for transient auth refreshes, but it's a breaking behavioral change for some integrators. We should recommend pinning and publish a compatibility note.

rami: For on-prem/dedicated customers we can also add a server-side check to dedupe identical incoming requests using idempotency header. Short-term I can enable stricter dedupe for this tenant if they want.

sophia: Customer wants a quick workaround. I'll ask them to pin and apply retry_policy=max_retries=0. Also asked them to rotate token TTL while we triage.

support-bot: Ticket SUP-4321 created and linked to eng issue #ENG-8765.

maria: Plan: revert aggressive 401 immediate retry in a bugfix release 1.31.1 with opt-in 'retry_mode="aggressive"' flag for customers who prefer it. I'll open a PR to restore legacy default and add feature flag.

maria: PR will include release note snippet and migration guidance: pin to <=1.29.3 OR set RetryPolicy(max_retries=0) as a workaround.

alex: Also add a quick KB blurb in support docs with exact pip command: `pip install redwood==1.29.3` and a note about double-billing risk.

sophia: Thanks. I'll relay to customer and confirm whether they want us to enable server-side dedupe. If they do, rami will toggle.

rami: I can enable tenant dedupe for a 24h window. Ping me in the ticket and I'll do it.

sophia: Closing loop here for now — recommended customer pin to 1.29.3 and apply RetryPolicy workaround. Follow-up ENG triage in #ENG-8765.

maria: I'll also add an automated test covering auth-refresh+retry paths so this doesn't regress.

sophia: Great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
